summary: Project Jupiter is Oracle's 2.5 GW data centre campus in the Santa Teresa area of Doña Ana County, New Mexico. The financing runs through county industrial revenue bonds under Ordinance 367-2025: a $165 billion authorization ceiling that reconciles as Series 2025A of $15 billion, Series 2025B of $25 billion and Series 2025C of about $125 billion. The county holds title and leases the project back to the project companies, which is why the county assessor shows no parcels in the campus parties' names. The bonds are private placements. No CUSIP, fund holder position or trade print for any Jupiter entity appears in the record, and EMMA carries no continuing disclosure for them.

Power is the contested point. The Community Benefits Agreement signed on November 12, 2025 commits the project, in Exhibit A, Section 8.4, to power itself with an onsite microgrid system. Oracle has since pursued two supply routes the county disputes or regulators have blocked: the Green Chile gas pipeline, rejected at state level in July 2026 and now before FERC, and a supplemental grid connection from El Paso Electric, which the county commission voted on October 27, 2026 to treat as a potential breach of the IRB agreements. The $165 billion figure is an authorization ceiling across the three series, not a project cost. The record holds no total project cost and no construction status beyond the reported 2028 online target.

summary: Hyperion is Meta's flagship AI data center campus in Richland Parish, Louisiana, a 2,250-acre site announced in December 2024 at an initially reported cost above $10 billion. In October 2025 Meta moved the campus into a joint venture owned 80 percent by funds managed by Blue Owl Capital and 20 percent by Meta, with about $27 billion of committed development costs; Blue Owl funds contributed about $7 billion in cash and Meta received a one-time distribution of about $3 billion.

The venture's issuer, Beignet Investor LLC, sold $27.294 billion of 6.581 percent senior secured notes due May 30, 2049 in October 2025, the largest single-tranche private debt offering on record. Meta leases the campus under operating leases with a four-year initial term and extension options, backed by a residual value guarantee covering roughly the first 16 years. In July 2026 Meta announced an expansion to 5 GW, taking total planned investment above $50 billion.

summary: Helios is Galaxy Digital's data center campus in Dickens County, West Texas, converted from a Bitcoin mining site Galaxy acquired from Argo Blockchain in December 2022 for about $65 million. CoreWeave is the sole tenant for Helios I: 526 MW of critical IT load across three phases, using 800 MW of gross power, each phase on a 15-year base lease term.

Phase I (133 MW) was completed and fully delivered to CoreWeave by July 2026. Phase II (260 MW) is under construction, financed in July 2026 with $3.507 billion of 9.875 percent senior secured notes due 2031 issued by Galaxy Helios Data Centers II LLC, with data hall deliveries scheduled to begin in the second quarter of 2027. The campus holds 1.63 GW of ERCOT-approved gross power, including a further 830 MW approved in January 2026 that was not under lease at the third quarter of 2026.
